title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Minimal Novel Information and Field-Level Independence
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — минимальная новая информация и независимость на уровне полей

scan_scope: selected state, memory, receipt and provenance records

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: MINIMAL_NEW_INFORMATION_UNIT
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: The smallest defensible component of a record that contributes information not already contained in the dependency closure of its parent, source event, or correlated derivative artifacts.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: What information does this JSON actually add that was not already present upstream?
primary_hidden_node_candidate.why_tenth_order: After collapsing shared registry dependencies and underlying events, the next unit of independence may be neither a file nor an event but the smallest genuinely new observation or measurement-bearing field.

emergent_invariants.name: FILE_NOVELTY_IS_NOT_INFORMATION_NOVELTY
emergent_invariants.description: A new JSON can add formatting, provenance, interpretation, hashing, or supersession metadata without adding a new observation about the underlying subject.

emergent_invariants.name: FIELD_LEVEL_DEPENDENCE
emergent_invariants.pattern: NEW_FIELD := NEW_INFORMATION ONLY IF OUTSIDE DEPENDENCY_CLOSURE
emergent_invariants.description: A record may contain a mixture of inherited fields and genuinely new measurements. Independence should therefore sometimes be evaluated at field or claim level rather than file level.

emergent_invariants.name: DERIVED_COMPUTATION_IS_NOT_NEW_OBSERVATION
emergent_invariants.description: Multiple analyses computed from the same raw observation can provide useful robustness checks but do not create independent observations merely by using different code or formulas.

emergent_invariants.name: MINIMAL_SUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
emergent_invariants.description: Connection support should ideally be represented by the smallest set of independent information-bearing units sufficient to reproduce the claimed relation.

emergent_invariants.name: REDUNDANCY_AND_INDEPENDENCE_ARE_DUALS
emergent_invariants.description: Redundant artifacts can improve integrity, auditability, or error detection while simultaneously contributing little or no additional independence. Reliability and independence must therefore be reported separately.

connections.machine_observation: Across very different data objects, the most useful claims are repeatedly bounded by identifying what is directly observed, what is inferred, what is inherited from prior state, and what still requires measurement.
connections.pattern_description: The useful unit of a Connection may be a newly measured property or state transition, not the whole JSON container that describes it.
connections.why_non_obvious: The files differ radically in subject matter, but their epistemic payloads can be decomposed into inherited context plus a small set of new information-bearing claims.
alternative_explanations: This may simply be a consequence of evidence-first writing style.
Some contextual fields may themselves carry independent information and should not be discarded mechanically.
connections.falsification_route: Annotate each field as inherited, transformed, observed, independently measured, or interpretive and test whether Connection rankings remain stable when only new-information fields are retained.

connections.machine_observation: Tranception bounds its score as a fitness estimate; the SCOBY protocol blocks reinforcement claims until material identity, incorporation and property effects are measured; the Connection scans similarly separate detection from validation.
connections.pattern_description: A recurring operator is to preserve a typed boundary between a measurable output and the stronger claim that someone might want to infer from it.
connections.why_non_obvious: The same logical separation appears across protein modeling, materials testing, and meta-analysis without requiring shared subject matter.
alternative_explanations: All three records were written under similar evidence-first conventions.
The pattern may be standard scientific hygiene rather than a distinctive JANUS relation.
connections.falsification_route: Compare with unrelated data schemas and measure whether the same typed separation appears at similar frequency without JANUS-style evidence boundaries.

connections.machine_observation: Across sequence modeling, capsule architecture and fictional state forensics, stored or retrieved state is treated as distinct from the live state currently being judged.
connections.pattern_description: The same structural problem recurs: memory, retrieval, persistence or exported state can inform interpretation without automatically proving present identity, present function, or present condition.
connections.why_non_obvious: These records span biological sequence prediction, embedded-system architecture and game forensics. The common element is the state-transition graph, not the subject.
alternative_explanations: State persistence and identity checks are common engineering patterns.
The fictional forensic records may have been explicitly influenced by the same engineering questions as the capsule architecture.
connections.falsification_route: Remove narrative labels and compare only state transition primitives across unrelated stateful systems; test whether the same separation remains.

source_objects: selected hash, receipt and report families
connections.machine_observation: Hashes, receipts, versions, reports and repeated analyses can make a record more auditable while remaining descendants of the same information source.
connections.pattern_description: The repository repeatedly separates integrity/reliability from independent information. JANUS now treats that separation as a first-class Connection feature.
connections.why_non_obvious: Redundant machine evidence feels like more evidence to a human reader even when it contains no new source information.
alternative_explanations: Some redundant artifacts can detect independent classes of failure and thus add reliability without adding source independence.
A simple independence metric may undercount useful orthogonal validation.
connections.falsification_route: Score each derivative artifact along two axes: new information and new failure-mode coverage. Verify that reliability gains can occur without increasing source independence.

connections.machine_observation: After event-level and derivative-level collapse, the next natural reduction is to keep only the smallest source-event and information-bearing units needed to reproduce a candidate relation.
connections.pattern_description: Connection analysis can evolve from a large archive graph into a minimal graph where each retained node has an explicit reason for existing: independent source event, new observation, validator of a distinct failure mode, or external witness.
connections.why_non_obvious: The repository naturally accumulates rich provenance; a minimal graph can look weaker while actually being more epistemically calibrated.
alternative_explanations: Minimalization can erase useful context needed to understand why a relationship exists.
A single minimal graph may not be sufficient for all Connection types.
connections.falsification_route: Compare candidate rankings from full graphs against minimal graphs and evaluate whether high-value edges remain stable while derivative-only edges disappear.

tenth_order_graph.candidate_hidden_path: RAW_SOURCE -> GENERATING_EVENT -> collapse derivatives -> classify fields -> retain NEW_INFORMATION_UNIT -> compare against CURRENT_STATE -> emit MINIMAL_CONNECTION_EDGE
tenth_order_graph.critical_prediction: A large fraction of apparent Connection support will collapse when only genuinely new information-bearing units are retained.
tenth_order_graph.counter_prediction: High-value connections that remain after event, derivative, field and representation collapse have a stronger claim to source-level residual structure.

next_scan_strategy.name: FIELD_LEVEL_CONNECTION_BENCHMARK
next_scan_strategy.target: Build an explicit field-level information ancestry map for high-value Connection candidates.
tests: FIELD_CLASSIFICATION: observed, derived, inherited, interpretive, metadata, provenance, validation.
FIELD_DEPENDENCY: map every field to its parent source field or generating event.
NEW_INFORMATION_FILTER: retain only fields that add information not already in the dependency closure.
CURRENT_VS_STORED_STATE: separate historical/retrieved state from direct present-state observations.
REDUNDANCY_VS_FAILURE_COVERAGE: record whether a derivative adds a new failure-mode check even when it adds no source information.
MINIMAL_GRAPH REBUILD: construct a graph from independent events and new-information units only.
CROSS_REPRESENTATION CHECK: repeat on a representation designed independently of the JANUS Connection vocabulary.
EXTERNAL_CHECK: where applicable, reproduce the minimal edge from an external source environment.
next_scan_strategy.promotion_rule: Do not promote a Connection because the JSON is large, repeated, richly hashed, or recursively documented. Promote only the smallest defensible independent information-bearing structure that survives the relevant dependency controls.

limitations: This scan proposes a more granular unit of analysis but does not yet construct a complete field-level ancestry map for the entire repository.
Field-level independence can be ambiguous when a derived field combines multiple source events.
Some current-state questions legitimately require historical state, so stored-state removal can produce false negatives if applied blindly.
No connection in this scan establishes truth, causality, novelty, or external replication.
canonical_rule: The deepest useful unit of Connection is not the file. It is the smallest independently informative change or observation that survives its dependency closure.
